newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 17.

text.p: General Motors Corp agreed to sell the defense businesses of its Hughes Electronics Corp unit to Raytheon Co for $9.5 billion in stock and debt. Northrop Grumman Corp, a rival suitor, is left in a tough, but not dire position, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
Other stories in the paper included:
* Financial services legislation faces fewer obstacles toward passage this year, lawmakers and the administration told the paper.
* A Samuel Zell real estate investment trust agreed to buy a rival apartment firm for $620 million, plus assumed debt.
* Fidelity Investment will double its offering of index funds this year.
* General Electric Co profits matched Wall Street's fourth quarter expectations.
* Eastman Kodak Co will cut 3,900 jobs and took a $256 million charge to cover the restructuring. Fourth quarter operating results improved before the charge.
* Digital Equipment Corp's fiscal second quarter profits fell, compared with last year's second quarter's results, but the firm topped analysts' expectations.
* The Dow Jones Industrial Average set a new record at 6,765.37. Bond prices fell.
* Federated Department Stores Inc's chief executive resigned unexpectedly.
* The chairman of Mercedes Benz, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, resigned.
* Conrail Inc appeared to be losing a shareholder vote in its agreement to merge with CSX Corp. Norfolk Southern Corp is offering a rival bid for Conrail.
* America Online Inc will curb marketing spending and spend more on upgrading its network.
* R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co faces new documents in a racial discrimination suit.
* Home video revenues rose 17 percent in 1996.
* HEARD ON THE STREET: Barclays Global Investors is the number two U.S. money manager ranked by assets, building its status via index mutual funds.
